hook: Several independent firms could build one trusted brand without handing their future to a single owner.
readerPromise: Understand a brand as shared institutional power and explore what meaningful decentralization would require.
protectedRevelations: Detailed proposed legal and constitutional arrangements
visualPlan: Who owns the shared future?: Show two separate workshops placing the same trusted name beside their own doors. Place a shared charter between the workshops while each keeps its own tools, work and decisions.
A name becomes a promise: Let a customer point to a promise on the shared charter and a member listen. Move between the shared name and the two independent workplaces without merging their buildings.

The powers behind participation: Place proposed rule change, membership decision and sale request before more than one member. Keep the shared record, common resources and usable separate exit route visible together.

Follow the common name: Contrast a single owner's control with a membership discussion where the shared charter actually constrains decisions. End on the charter between the workshops, with members still able to choose their own work.

cueChanges.nextVisualChange: Keep several contributors connected to one recognizable name, with the decision point visibly separate.
Use a guild mark and contemporary shared identity as distinct historical moments.
Reduce governance choreography to one rule change and one possible exit, without suggesting that a vote resolves ownership.
End with the shared promise still between autonomous participants and the reader’s book.

sentenceIntentions.text: Several independent firms could build one trusted brand without handing their future to a single owner.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Offer autonomous firms sharing a trusted brand as the specific proposal
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Imagine cooperation without surrender to one owner

sentenceIntentions.text: Decentralised Brands proposes shared rules for that name while its members keep control of their own work.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the shared-rules proposal and retained autonomy
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the proposal before considering its background

sentenceIntentions.text: The proposal treats a brand as a promise that customers and members can hold one another to.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give shared branding a promise that members and customers can invoke
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize a concrete obligation beyond using the same logo

sentenceIntentions.text: A shared name can carry trust, memory, and belonging without making every participant part of one company.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Distinguish shared reputation from becoming one corporation
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See how common identity could coexist with separate work

sentenceIntentions.text: The hard question is who may change the rules, remove a member, or sell what everyone helped build.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Expose the contested powers a shared identity must settle
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Become curious about who truly controls the name

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows those powers through ownership, records, common resources, and the practical freedom to leave.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Trace those powers into resources, records and meaningful exit
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize what autonomy would need in practice

sentenceIntentions.text: Its promise is worth testing against both corporate control and communities that share a name but little authority.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Set the proposal against both ownership concentration and superficial sharing
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Expect a proposal to test rather than a slogan to admire

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin with the shared promise, and ask which decisions must truly belong to the members.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Invite scrutiny of the members' actual decision rights
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to inspect which rules make the shared promise real

distinctiveContribution: The book proposes a brand shared by autonomous firms or other participants under explicit limits, rather than a name one owner can sell or control.
